 Counsel for the respondents : Mr. B.S. Parihar, learned Additional

B.P.S. Mer, learned Standing

The Court made the following:
JUDGMENT: (per Sri Manoj Kumar Gupta, C.J.)

1) The case is listed under the caption "Fresh
Cases as Defective". The defect, as pointed out by the
Registry, being negligible, is hereby ignored.
2) The petitioner was one of the bidders to a
tender process initiated by the respondent-department for
outsourcing manpower. The petitioner along with private
respondent No. 3 were declared L1 as is evident from the
1

UKHC010151732026
2026:UHC:8367-DB
screen shot of the GeM Portal filed at page 56 of the writ
petition. The case of the petitioner is that respondent No.
3 was not having experience of 05 similar works with the
Government department which was an essential eligibility
condition. It is also his case that barely two months back
a bid submitted by respondent No. 3 in respect of some
other contract was declared non-responsive on the said
ground. However, in the present case, the department
had declared respondent No. 3 as technically qualified.
The petitioner is stated to have filed objections against the
declaration of the bid of respondent No. 3 as technically
qualified and since the objection has not been decided,
the present writ petition has been filed, questioning the
award of contract in favour of the private respondent.
3) Learned State counsel states that the
representation of the petitioner dated 21.08.2026 filed in
this regard shall be decided by the department.
4) Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on
merits, the writ petition is disposed of with direction to the
department to decide the representation dated
21.08.2026 after affording opportunity of hearing to
private respondent No. 3 within a period of four weeks
from the date of communication of the instant order.
2

5) Pending applications(s), if any, also stand
disposed of.
